caveats: ⚑ Both shield-gated blocks (S1 core +85.17%, burst ATK +31.02%) are INERT unless another unit sets a shield on naga — her own kit sets none. On a comp with no shielder the modeled contribution collapses to the S2 core buff + the 16.18% burst ATK. Uptime is entirely a function of the ally shielder's cadence; requiresShielded has no duration decay here because the shield source is external.

⚑ S1 trigger identity: the kit gives the core buff an activation clause ('when a Shield is set') but naga cannot self-satisfy it. Authored as passive+requiresShielded (continuous while shielded) rather than a shield-application trigger with a 10s window — these diverge whenever the ally shield is intermittent. If the engine has a shield-application trigger, the 10s duration implies the buff should REFRESH per shield application, not hold continuously.

⚑ hitCount semantics for a 10-pellet SG: 'after 12 / 5 normal attack(s)' is authored as ROUNDS (trigger pulls), per the schema's 'counts ROUNDS not pulls' note read as one-bullet-per-pull for a non-MG. If the engine counts SG pellet HITS instead, the 5-hit S2 fires ~10x more often (every ~half shot) and the buff becomes permanent uptime rather than intermittent — a large swing in the S2 core buff's effective value.
⚑ coreDamagePct stacking: S1 (85.17%) and S2 (40.07%) both land on the same stat for overlapping ally sets; assumed additive in the core bucket with no cap. Not stated in the kit.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Naga is a core-damage supporter: two coreDamagePct grants (S1 all-allies 85.17%/10s shield-gated, S2 top-2-ATK 40.07%/5s on every 5 normals) plus a burst caster-scaled ATK grant that doubles (16.18% → +31.02%) while shielded. Both shield-gated blocks use requiresShielded and are inert without an external shielder — this is the single largest uncertainty in the model. The S1 Cover-HP restore is unmodeled (v1 has no cover-HP pool and it is not a unit heal, so it emits no recovery event); the S2 lowest-HP heal IS modeled as a heal effect per the tandem rule, since it drives teammates' on-recovery triggers even though no HP pool exists. Burst Pierce is a gainPierce effect (10s, self) rather than the whole-fight hasPierce flag, because the kit scopes it to the burst window. FB-by-timing left default ON; noFb not set (unmeasured).

audit.effectOrReason: Trigger for the Cover-HP line only; its sole effect is unmodeled, so no block carries the hitCount:12 trigger.
Cover HP is not modeled in v1 (no cover pool). NOT a 'heal' effect — cover restoration does not emit a unit recovery event, so it cannot drive on-recovery consumers. Verbatim in unmodeled.skill1.

audit.effectOrReason: second allies block, buff casterAtkPct 31.02, durationSec 10, requiresShielded:true. Authored as ADDITIVE to the 16.18% line (separate kit line, separate block), not a replacement.

flags.estimate: 0% uptime on a shielder-less comp; ~100% uptime with any shield-carrying ally in the team
flags.reasoning: Naga's own kit contains no 'shield' effect, so both shield-gated lines depend entirely on an external ally. The schema's requiresShielded gate treats a no-duration shield as permanent at scope (boss damage unmodeled, nothing breaks shields), so a single ally shield application flips both blocks fully on for the rest of the fight. This makes naga's modeled value bimodal — roughly 85.17 core + 31.02 caster-ATK swing between the two states — and any board-fit done on the wrong comp will mis-calibrate her.
flags.recipe: Run the standard control comp twice: once as-is, once with a shielder present. Diff the buffApply stream for stat coreDamagePct value 85.17 and stat casterAtkPct value ≈ (31.02/100)×naga.staticAtk. Then verify against footage whether the in-game core buff persists after the ally shield expires or drops with it — if it persists 10s from application, re-key skill1[0] to a shield-application trigger with durationSec 10 instead of a passive gate.

flags.estimate: passive (continuous while shielded); alternative = shield-application trigger refreshing a 10s window
flags.reasoning: The kit states both an activation event ('when a Shield is set in front of this unit') AND a 10s duration. Those two readings diverge: a passive+gate holds the buff for as long as the shield is up, while a per-application trigger holds it exactly 10s per shield cast. With an intermittent ally shielder (e.g. a burst-cadence shield every ~20s) the passive reading over-credits by roughly the fraction of the cycle beyond 10s. I chose passive because the schema has no 'shielded' trigger kind exposed in the redacted TriggerDef I was given (the requiresShielded comment mentions a distinct 'shielded' TRIGGER exists, but it is not in the TriggerDef union here) — so the gate is the only expressible form.
flags.recipe: Confirm whether a 'shielded' trigger kind exists in the unredacted types.ts. If it does, author skill1[0] with that trigger + durationSec 10 and compare total damage against the passive+gate form on a comp whose shielder has a >10s cadence; the delta is the size of this error. Footage check: watch whether naga's core-buff icon expires 10s after the shield lands or tracks the shield's own bar.

flags.estimate: 5 trigger pulls (~0.55 magazines of her 9-round belt); 12 pulls for the unmodeled S1 line
flags.reasoning: Naga is an SG with hitsPerShot 10, so 'normal attack' is ambiguous between one trigger pull (10 pellets) and one pellet hit. The schema comment on hitCount says it 'counts ROUNDS not pulls', which for an MG means hitsPerShot rounds per pull — but for an SG the ammo economy spends 1 round per pull while 10 pellets land. If the engine counts pellet landings, the 5-threshold fires roughly every half shot and the 5s core buff becomes permanent-uptime; if it counts pulls, it fires every 5 shots (~2 per magazine) and the 5s window covers well under half the fight. This is the largest cadence uncertainty in the model.
flags.recipe: Instrument a solo run with cfg.onEvent, count shot events between consecutive buffApply events for stat coreDamagePct value 40.07, and compare that spacing to naga's pulls-per-second and 9-round magazine. 5 shots between applications confirms the rounds reading; sub-shot spacing confirms the pellet reading. Cross-check the S2 buff's real uptime against footage of her core-buff icon.

flags.estimate: additive, uncapped: up to 125.24 combined core-damage points on the top-2-ATK allies while shielded
flags.reasoning: Two separate kit lines grant coreDamagePct to overlapping ally sets with different durations (10s all-allies, 5s top-2). The kit says nothing about interaction. The schema's default for same-stat buffs from different blocks is assumed additive within the core bucket. If the game instead takes the maximum, or caps core-damage contribution, the modeled top-2 allies are over-credited by the smaller term.
flags.recipe: Read a fight where both windows are provably live and compare a core-hit popup on a top-2-ATK ally against the same ally's core popup with only one window active. The ratio distinguishes additive (both terms present) from max-only (only 85.17 present). Requires a shielded comp to open the S1 window at all.

flags.estimate: additive — both apply while shielded, total 47.20% of caster ATK
flags.reasoning: The kit lists these as two separate ■ blocks with independent activation clauses (one unconditional, one shield-gated), which normally means both land. The alternative reading is that the shielded line is an upgraded REPLACEMENT of the base line, giving 31.02% total rather than 47.20%. Nothing in the prose disambiguates. I chose additive because separate ■ headers are separate effects everywhere else in this schema's conventions.
flags.recipe: On a shielded comp, sum the buffApply events with stat casterAtkPct and casterIdx = naga's index at burst cast; two distinct flat-ATK applications (≈0.1618×staticAtk and ≈0.3102×staticAtk) confirm additive, one confirms replacement. Footage alternative: compare an ally's ATK stat readout across a shielded vs unshielded burst.

flags.estimate: self-only, 10s from burst cast, no damage of its own
flags.reasoning: Pierce is only worth damage if naga or a teammate carries a pierceDamagePct buff, which is inert in v1 per the StatKey comment. So this line is very likely damage-neutral in the current engine — but it must still be authored as gainPierce rather than dropped, since a future pierce consumer would silently miss it. Flagged because 'modeled but inert' is a state worth recording explicitly rather than discovering later.
flags.recipe: Grep the roster for any override carrying pierceDamagePct; if none is simSupported, confirm this block contributes exactly zero by diffing total damage with and without burst[0]. Re-check whenever a pierce consumer lands.

flags.estimate: datamined values taken as given; effective fire rate subject to the 60fps frame-boundary rounding
flags.reasoning: Per the ALWAYS-⚑ taxonomy, rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable datamine fields, and naga's entire trigger economy (both hitCount thresholds) rides on shots-per-second. An error here scales the S2 core-buff uptime linearly and shifts the unmodeled S1 line's cadence too.
flags.recipe: Read naga's ammo counter frame-by-frame in footage to get shots/sec directly (the instrument that measures the disputed quantity), rather than inferring it from burst-gauge or FB counts. Compare against 60/ceil(60/nominal).
